title: Dhamaal 4 Just Dropped Its Trailer Off a Literal Waterfall. The Franchise Has Never Known Chill.
excerpt: Ajay Devgn, Arshad Warsi, Riteish Deshmukh, and Jaaved Jaaferi reunite for a fourth treasure hunt — and they've brought Ravi Kishan, Esha Gupta, and Sanjay Mishra along for the chaos.
body:
The original *Dhamaal* quartet hasn't aged a day. They've just gotten louder.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=IG-eByZdz6Y</youtube>

The official trailer for **Dhamaal 4** dropped on Thursday, and the makers didn't just release it — they staged an entire event at **Imagicaa** amusement park outside Mumbai, where a massive 60-foot poster of the film cascaded down a grand waterfall while the full cast stood below, grinning like they'd already found the treasure. It was gloriously, unapologetically extra. Which, if you know this franchise, is exactly the point.

https://www.instagram.com/reel/DZfHMfdoqfb/

The trailer opens with **Upendra Limaye** dangling off a mountain cliff, being interrogated about the location of Shaitan Singh's fortune. If the first *Dhamaal* in 2007 sent the boys racing across Goa for ₹10 crore buried under the letter "W," this time the stakes are bigger — an even larger haul, hidden beneath the letter "M." What follows is three minutes of the franchise doing what it does best: organized chaos performed by actors who've been doing this together long enough to read each other's rhythms blindfolded.

**Ajay Devgn** leads with that signature deadpan — the man who delivers punchlines like they're business transactions. He's never been the one chasing laughs in these films; the laughs chase him. **Arshad Warsi**, meanwhile, remains Bollywood's most precise comic actor. His timing hasn't slipped in nearly two decades, and the trailer gives him at least three moments that land with surgical efficiency. **Riteish Deshmukh** throws himself into the physical bits with the commitment of someone who genuinely enjoys getting hit by things, and **Jaaved Jaaferi** — always the most underrated of the four — continues to mine absurdist gold from every situation the script hands him.

The new ensemble raises the energy. **Ravi Kishan**, in the middle of a remarkable career upswing, brings his raw Bhojpuri energy to the mix and looks right at home among the veterans. **Sanjay Mishra** — an actor who can make a single reaction shot funnier than an entire comedy special — appears in what looks like a scene-stealing role. **Esha Gupta** plays Devgn's wife and brings a no-nonsense glamour that the franchise hasn't had before. **Sanjeeda Shaikh** and **Anjali Anand** round out the women's roles, and both appear to have been given actual parts to play — a quiet but welcome upgrade from earlier installments.

The visual comparisons to *Pirates of the Caribbean* are already circulating online, and they're not entirely unearned. The trailer's water sequences and jungle-set action pieces are the most visually ambitious the franchise has attempted. Director **Indra Kumar**, who created this world 19 years ago, has clearly been given a budget to match his ambitions this time around, and the production values — courtesy of **T-Series**, **Devgn Films**, **Maruti International**, and **Panorama Studios** — show in every frame.

For the Indian diaspora, *Dhamaal* occupies a very specific niche: it's the film your entire family can watch together without anyone needing to leave the room during an awkward scene. Clean comedy, recognizable faces, physical humor that transcends subtitle lag. If you've ever been at a desi house party where some uncle starts quoting "Ye Baburao ka style hai," you already know the cultural currency this franchise carries. The film will release internationally, and for NRI families looking for a clean, high-energy Bollywood night out this summer, July 10 is now circled in red.

The franchise's treasure-hunt formula — which has been its backbone since 2007 — now spans what appears to be multiple countries and terrains. The trailer promises the kind of relentless, high-energy slapstick that turns a multiplex into a laugh track, and with this ensemble, the comedy is less about individual moments and more about the collective chemistry that only comes from years of doing this together.

*Dhamaal 4* arrives in cinemas on **July 10, 2026** — strategically placed as a solo release after the Cocktail 2, Welcome to the Jungle, and Alpha wave has passed. By then, audiences will be ready for something that doesn't ask to be taken seriously. The *Dhamaal* boys have never once made that mistake, and they're clearly not starting now.
